title: Use of a Rat Model to Study Ventral Abdominal Hernia Repair
protocol: Acquire pathogen-free Sprague Dawley rats from a reputable vendor or breeding colony.
Ensure that the animals are clinically healthy one day prior to surgery.
Administer 1.1 - 1.2 mg/kg of sustained release buprenorphine subcutaneously to the rat 2 hours before surgery.
Apply ophthalmic ointment to both eyes.
Administer 2 mL of warmed sterile physiological saline subcutaneously.
Anesthetize the rat with an intraperitoneal dose of ketamine hydrochloride (90 mg/kg) and xylazine (10 mg/kg).
Apply a small amount of ocular lubricant to each eye to prevent corneal dessication.
Shave the ventral abdomen from the pubis to the sternum and laterally using commercial clippers.
Remove clipped hair by applying a moist paper towel to the area.
Scrub the shaved area with an iodophor antiseptic.
Wipe the scrubbed area with 70% ethanol.
Apply surgical drapes to isolate the incision window from contamination.
Don a sterile surgical gown, face mask, and hair bonnet.
Thoroughly wash hands with soap.
Scrub hands with soap.
Don sterile surgical gloves.
Using a scalpel, make an approximately 3 - 4 cm vertical incision along the ventral midline down to the level of the abdominal musculature.
Lift the abdominal wall gently with a forceps and create a small opening through the linea alba.
Insert a forceps through the hole into the abdominal cavity as a protective guide.
Incise the muscle wall to create an approximately 2 cm x 2 cm full thickness defect, cutting approximately 1 cm lateral from each side of the midline on both ends of the linea alba incision.
Lay a pre-cut 2 cm x 2 cm section of mechanical bridging material over the defect.
Suture the four corners of the bridging material to the abdominal wall muscle using 4-0 silk or nylon in a simple interrupted suture pattern.
Secure each edge of the material with three additional sutures spaced equally.
Examine the entire circumferential edge to ensure that significant gaps do not exist.
Place additional sutures if necessary to secure any gaps and prevent passage of viscera through the abdominal wall.
Close the subcutaneous tissue with 4-0 absorbable suture in a simple interrupted pattern.
Close the skin with surgical staples.
Keep the animal in a warm area until it has regained sufficient consciousness to regain sternal recumbency.
Examine animals daily after surgery to ensure full recovery and normal healing.
Remove skin staples with a staple remover 7 - 10 days following surgery.
Euthanize animals with carbon dioxide overdose administered at a chamber fill rate of 10 to 30%.
Open the skin and abdominal wall using standard necropsy tools.
Expose the area of the implant.
Observe any gross pathological observations including adverse reactions.
Remove the implant site by cutting a wide section of tissue that includes the implant.
Place the sample in 10% neutral buffered formalin.
Prepare the sample for histological examination and characterization.
